name: Daventry aircraft radio-detection demonstration
description: A 1935 British field demonstration detected an aircraft through its effect on radio signals.

impact.note: One field trial seen by a handful of officials, proving a known effect usable; British radar development and the Chain Home line were funded directly on it.

earliest_record.rationale: The report is a dated witness preceding or accompanying the demonstrated instance; the sources do not establish a global first.

caveats: This event demonstrated a detectable aircraft-related signal, not a measurement of aircraft range or a complete operational warning system. The RAF history says the trial preceded a request for Treasury approval of NPL research; no funding or payment for this trial is inferred.

research.note: The Science Museum’s distance figure is contextual and is not recorded as a measurement of ranging. Only broad historical descriptions of the test are retained. Independent review checked the NPL history, Science Museum object description and RAF retrospective, including their stated participant roles and the trial’s inability to locate the aircraft.
